subject.title: fix(codex): omit idle PreToolUse hook relays

question: Should Codex sessions with unset tools.loopDetection stop installing loop-detection-only native PreToolUse command hooks by default, or should OpenClaw preserve the old default and expose only an explicit opt-out/configured mitigation?
rationale: The code is reviewable, but choosing the default changes the upgrade contract for native Codex tool hooks and determines whether the linked P1 issue can be closed by this narrow mitigation.

options.title: Accept scoped default change
options.body: Merge this PR as the default idle-relay mitigation, while explicitly leaving broader relay concurrency or explicit loopDetection work tracked if needed.

options.title: Prefer default-preserving opt-out
options.body: Pause this PR and use a config-based or policy-based path so existing unset loopDetection behavior does not change on upgrade.

options.title: Wait for broader relay design
options.body: Pause both narrow mitigations until maintainers choose concurrency caps, a lightweight relay entrypoint, or a resident relay design.

recommendation.title: Accept scoped default change
recommendation.body: Merge this PR as the default idle-relay mitigation, while explicitly leaving broader relay concurrency or explicit loopDetection work tracked if needed.

likelyOwner.reason: Current file history and related discussion both point to this person for the compatibility/default-surface choice.
